contents.text: I'm not sure where the tool loop card sits on the how-it-works page, so I won't guess a path. I'll skip looking it up and just answer, offering the user a few options.

The engine runs each tool call itself, in a loop, and every call passes the guards before it runs. Here is the sequence for one message:

1. The engine sends the model your message, the chat so far, and the tools for the session.
2. If the model answers with a tool call, the engine logs it and runs it through the guards.
3. The tool's result goes back to the model as the next message in the conversation.
4. The model either answers or asks for more tools. This repeats for up to 10 rounds per message.
5. The answer streams back as it is written, and the whole turn is kept in the history.

The guards do three things. A result over 50,000 characters is summarised by a separate model call with no tools, so one tool can't flood the context. A call cut off by the 16,000-token output limit is never run, and the model is asked to write large content in chunks. A tool that throws sends its exception message back to the model, which can correct itself.

Tool arguments are passed as data, never pasted into a shell command. Each public method on a pack's tool class becomes a tool, and the engine registers only the toolsets the session names.

Source: `src/docs/architecture/06-runtime-view.md`, under "A chat turn", "Guards around tool calls" and "A turn, step by step".
